argument_markdown:
## Source-backed inputs

ATT-0065, confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109, supplies the canonical filtered balanced CE quotient W5 and the scheme-theoretic identification of the intrinsic evaluation-failure locus on Conf6 with the relative-triviality/Abel–Jacobi incidence (CLM-0065-4, CLM-0065-5 and CLM-0065-9). ATT-0066, confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116, supplies the global Abel–Jacobi model and the stack-level finite étale S6 ordering torsor on distinct support (CLM-0066-5 and CLM-0066-6). ATT-0086, confirmed by REV-0135 and REV-0138, excludes the balanced h0(L)=4 stratum. ATT-0088, confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142, gives under (CE)+(BAL)+(N) the identities L≅omega_C(-D), h0(O_C(D))=2 and h0(L)=3, fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support open, and, over a reduced base, the P2-bundle, smoothness, surjectivity, relative dimension two, and component-dimension statements (CLM-0088-1, CLM-0088-3, CLM-0088-5 and CLM-0088-8). The sign convention for W5 is the SRC-0004 convention already checked in those artifacts.

## Proved steps

First, the cited inputs identify I with the projectivization of the rank-three bundle pi_*L on the reduced base H. Thus I→H is a P2-bundle. Its distinct-support locus U meets every geometric fibre and is open and dense there. The ordering morphism Z→U is a finite étale S6-torsor, while ATT-0088 identifies Z with the intrinsic Fitting failure scheme and proves Z→H smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two. The component domination and formula dim T=dim H_alpha+2 are therefore exactly CLM-0088-8.

For the component count, let V be connected and normal and choose a geometric base point. Identifying one fibre of the S6-torsor with S6, étale monodromy acts by translations through a subgroup H_V⊂S6. Its orbits are the cosets of H_V, so there are [S6:H_V] connected components, each of degree |H_V|. A finite étale cover of a normal scheme is normal; the irreducible components of a locally Noetherian normal scheme are open and closed. Hence each connected component is irreducible, proving the stated irreducible-component count and dimension formula. No value of H_V is inferred.

Now fix a geometric point z=(C,gamma,x1,…,x6) and put Gamma=sum xi. Let D be a fibre divisor of gamma. The normalization and CLM-0088-1 give L≅omega_C(-D), while membership in Z gives O_C(Gamma)≅L. Therefore

omega_C(-Gamma)≅O_C(D)=gamma^*O_{P1}(1).

By CLM-0088-3, h0(O_C(D))=2. Pullback gives an injective map H0(P1,O(1))→H0(C,O_C(D)); both sides have dimension two, so it is an isomorphism. Thus gamma is precisely the morphism defined by the complete pencil |omega_C(-Gamma)|. Any second balanced normalized cover producing the same ordered pointed curve and satisfying the incidence condition is defined by the same complete pencil and therefore differs from gamma by a unique target automorphism. Uniqueness follows from surjectivity of gamma.

If alpha∈Aut(C,x1,…,x6), functoriality of omega_C and alpha(Gamma)=Gamma give an action on H0(C,omega_C(-Gamma)). Projectivizing supplies a target automorphism beta with beta∘gamma=gamma∘alpha. It is unique because gamma is surjective. Conversely every automorphism of the cover forgets to an automorphism of the ordered pointed curve. Hence Aut(C,gamma,x1,…,x6)→Aut(C,x1,…,x6) is an isomorphism. This proves both uniqueness of the geometric source object over a pointed curve and triviality of relative inertia; it does not assert either absolute stabilizer is trivial.

The inertia criterion for morphisms of algebraic stacks now makes u representable by algebraic spaces. Recovery over every algebraically closed extension makes the representable morphism universally injective. Since u is of finite type and every geometric fibre has at most one point, it is quasi-finite. For an irreducible component T, the dimension theorem for quasi-finite finite-type morphisms gives dim closure(u(T))=dim T. Combining this with dim T=dim H_alpha+2 yields the final conditional dimension statement; when dim H_alpha=15, the image closure has dimension 17 and hence codimension 21-17=4 in M_{6,6}.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment, point count, or computational sample is used.

## Remaining gaps and exact-target boundary

The weak normalization (N) remains an explicit hypothesis. Irreducibility, normality, and dimension 15 of the global balanced Hurwitz base are not proved, and the subgroup H_V is not computed. Universal injectivity plus inertia control is not promoted to full faithfulness on arbitrary base schemes or to a monomorphism. The image is not proved closed, pure, regular, or exhaustive of unbalanced evaluation failure. Therefore no Gysin, Hodge, weight, purity, Tate-support, or Tate-assembly conclusion follows, and RED-0001 remains unresolved.

claims.justification: This is the combination of the scheme-theoretic incidence identification from ATT-0065/REV-0108/REV-0109 with CLM-0088-5 and CLM-0088-8 from ATT-0088/REV-0139/REV-0142.
claims.statement: Over the reduced balanced normalized Hurwitz stack, the ordered failure incidence is smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two; each component dominates a Hurwitz component and has dimension two larger.

claims.justification: Monodromy orbits on the fibre S6 are cosets of H_V. They classify connected components of the finite étale cover; normality makes connected components irreducible.
claims.statement: For a connected normal base V, the irreducible components of the ordered S6-torsor are the monodromy cosets: their number is [S6:H_V], and each has degree |H_V| over V.

claims.justification: The identities O(Gamma)=L=omega(-D) give omega(-Gamma)=O(D). Since h0(O(D))=2, the pullback of H0(P1,O(1)) is the complete two-dimensional section space. Recovery and the automorphism comparison follow by projectivizing this canonical section space.
claims.statement: For every geometric balanced normalized failure point, |omega_C(-Gamma)| is the complete pencil defining gamma, and Aut(C,gamma,x1,…,x6)→Aut(C,x1,…,x6) is an isomorphism.

claims.justification: CLM-0096-3 gives injective geometric isomorphism classes and trivial relative inertia. The stack inertia criterion gives representability, the geometric-point criterion gives universal injectivity, finite type plus zero-dimensional geometric fibres gives quasi-finiteness, and the quasi-finite dimension theorem gives equality of dimensions.
claims.statement: The forgetful morphism u:Z→M_{6,6} is representable by algebraic spaces, universally injective, and quasi-finite; every component image closure has the same dimension as its source component.

novelty_claims: The fibrewise pencil-recovery identity is upgraded to an exact geometric inertia calculation and to representable, universally injective, quasi-finite behavior of the forgetful morphism, without claiming unproved full faithfulness on arbitrary families.
The finite étale ordering cover receives an exact irreducible-component formula over every connected normal base in terms of the actual, still-unknown monodromy subgroup.
summary: The balanced normalized marked curve determines its tetragonal pencil. This gives an exact geometric stabilizer comparison and makes the forgetful map representable, universally injective, and quasi-finite, while the ordered-cover components over a normal base are counted by monodromy cosets. The unknown Hurwitz components and monodromy image prevent a numerical global component count.

theorem_scope.base: An algebraically closed characteristic-zero field; H is assumed reduced and of finite type. The component count in clause (2) retains connectedness and normality.
theorem_scope.generality: The relative P2 geometry and smoothness are asserted only over the reduced balanced normalized Hurwitz stack. Pencil recovery, geometric-fibre uniqueness, and inertia comparison hold after every algebraically closed field extension. The quasi-finite conclusion uses that u is a finite-type morphism between finite-type algebraic stacks.
theorem_scope.hypotheses: (CE), (BAL), and the weak normalization (N) are explicit hypotheses. H is the moduli stack of covers modulo target isomorphism and carries no auxiliary choices whose scalars would create extra inertia. Z is the ordered distinct-support intrinsic evaluation-failure incidence.
theorem_scope.not_covered: Nonreduced bases; unbalanced splitting strata; irreducibility or dimension 15 of H; computation of H_V or full S6 monodromy; full faithfulness on arbitrary families or a stack monomorphism; triviality of Aut(C,x1,…,x6); closedness or component purity of the image; identification with the full evaluation-failure locus in M_{6,6}; closure through unbalanced strata; regular embedding or Gysin theory in M_{6,6}; Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, coarse-space, integral-coefficient, or positive-characteristic conclusions.

theorem_statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Let H be the reduced finite-type algebraic Hurwitz stack whose objects are smooth genus-six finite-flat degree-four covers gamma:C→P of a P1-bundle, modulo isomorphism of the target, satisfying (CE) the standard degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl resolution, (BAL) fibrewise F≅O(4)⊕O(5), and (N) the weak relative-canonical normalization used in ATT-0066 and ATT-0088. No target coordinates, splitting of F, normalization isomorphism, or trivialization of an Abel–Jacobi equality is included as object data. Let W5 be the canonical degree-16 quotient, L=W5⊗omega^{-1}, I the degree-six Abel–Jacobi incidence for L, U⊂I its distinct-support open, and Z=Ord(U) the ordered incidence, equivalently the intrinsic balanced CE evaluation-failure scheme on Conf6. Then: (1) I→H is a P2-bundle, U→H and Z→H are smooth and surjective of pure relative dimension two, and Z→U is a finite étale S6-torsor. Every irreducible component T of Z dominates an irreducible component H_alpha of H and dim T=dim H_alpha+2. (2) If V is a connected normal component of U and H_V⊂S6 is the image of the monodromy representation of Z_V→V, then Z_V has exactly [S6:H_V] irreducible components; each is finite étale of degree |H_V| over V and has dimension dim V. (3) The forgetful morphism u:Z→M_{6,6} recovers the tetragonal pencil on every geometric point: for z=(C,gamma,x1,…,x6), with Gamma=sum xi, the complete pencil |omega_C(-Gamma)| is gamma up to a unique target isomorphism. Consequently Aut(C,gamma,x1,…,x6)→Aut(C,x1,…,x6) is an isomorphism, and every geometric fibre of u has either no object or one isomorphism class with trivial relative automorphism group. (4) Hence u is representable by algebraic spaces, universally injective, and quasi-finite. For each irreducible component T⊂Z, dim closure(u(T))=dim T; in particular, if its dominated Hurwitz component has dimension 15, then closure(u(T)) has dimension 17 and codimension 4 in M_{6,6}. No monomorphism on arbitrary families, closed-immersion, purity, lci, Gysin, or numerical monodromy assertion is made.
